original_records.evidence: Hint C01:484 verified - the backtick is present, verbatim, at the head of both the ACIP and the Wylie. But it is not stray. The same leading backtick opens 111 segments across at least 15 courses (C09 x23, C13 x19, C18 x12, C17 x9, C08 x7, C07 x6, C01 x2, and more), and in every sampled case it introduces a new text, chapter, or titled section: C02:27 '`, , gnyis pa rang gi lugs la' = 'Here is the second section'; C06:24 '`, na mo ma{u2} o ShA ya' = 'I bow down to Manjughosha'; C09:142 '`, gnyis pa ni' under the heading 'the colophon'. Here it opens the Gungtang appendix, and the English confirms a fresh text begins: 'Here is a "Secret Key to the Three Principal Paths"'.
original_records.note: This is a structural marker in the ACIP e-text, functioning as a section/text-opening delimiter, not digitisation damage. The campaign was right to keep it verbatim and it should stay. Recommend the register carry it as a resolved non-issue so the same character is not re-flagged on later courses - C09 alone will raise it 23 more times. The trailing 'Layer: 3,747 headwords / 7,014 pairs' in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no claim about the text.

scope: Original registered-class record. Historical counts in its evidence were not independently remeasured by this preparation; no new erratum proposed.
